tier_reason: Lowered C to D: the only numbers come from a degenerate benchmark (fluid solver on all-zero fields with a data race on row 0 and a check that compares zeros with zeros, matmul results never reset, no -O3 applied, pool hard-coded to 4 workers), so nothing valid was measured; directional only, and the library is not faster than std::async per task in any case.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Red-Portal benchmark: +3.7% on a degenerate fluid solver and -15% on matmul vs std::async thread-per-task; no valid measurement.
corrections.caveats: fluid_solver.cpp never calls addInflow (zero fields), all 2048 row tasks write row 0 (data race), check_result vacuous; -O3 never applied; 4 hard-coded workers vs hardware_concurrency(); abandoned 2014-09-26; 1M trivial tasks 5 s (#84).

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Caveat correction: two correctness bugs in the general sort paths (SORT3/SORT4 networks and the s_msb radix split, the latter already in the 2017 benchmark code) leave only the 8-bit counting sort usable; the 32/64-bit rows were both slower and wrong.

corrections.caveats: 8-bit counting sort about 5.0-5.6x vs libstdc++ std::sort (2017 tables, g++ 5.2.1, i5-3330, -O2); 32/64-bit libsrt sorts 0.82-0.90x and incorrect (s_msb stops one shift short; SORT3/SORT4 networks wrong); bench and stest use only ascending, reversed or evens-then-odds input; ssort.c untouched since 2019; no upstream issue filed.

tier_reason: Tier stays A (Quill benchmark with public harness, compiler, flags and CPU). Caveat correction: the 4-thread Boost.Log rows in odygrd/logger_benchmarks race on a shared non-thread-safe src::severity_logger and are invalid; only the 1-thread rows (2.9-3.2x lower latency than Boost.Log) stand, and g3log remains 3-4x slower than spdlog.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 1 thread: 2.9-3.2x lower latency than Boost.Log (derived from page data); 4-thread Boost.Log rows invalid (data race in the harness); g3log second-slowest in the table and 3-4x slower than spdlog.
corrections.caveats: Call site about 1 us; unbounded queue with no backpressure; one thread per sink; fatal handler not async-signal-safe, SIGTERM treated as fatal; messages before initializeLogging dropped; reckless 186x over fstream is a NAS write storm; Unlicense, no patent grant.

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Correction: the benchmark code exists (examples/readme_perf_examples.cpp), but keep_if on a const lvalue is std::copy_if plus back_inserter itself, so the parity figure compares identical code, and the inverted numRuns guard makes Release builds run 10 iterations.

corrections.caveats: Parity, not faster (same code path as std::copy_if); numRuns guard inverted (10 iterations in Release); every call through std::function copying the 5000-int input; 16,100-line umbrella header.
